reason: While the narrative follows Moses (who will later become a leader), he is not yet established as a leader in this passage. He is a young man attempting to help his people. Moreover, the portrayal of the Hebrews is not characterized as ungrateful. When the Hebrew confronts Moses, asking 'Who made you a ruler and judge over us?' (verse 14), the issue is one of unauthorized intervention and lack of legitimacy, not ingratitude for received help or leadership. Moses has not yet provided leadership or assistance that would warrant accusations of ingratitude. The passage depicts rejection of his authority, not ingratitude to a recognized leader.
